weight loss was predicted by perceived control, which in turn was predicted by intention.
the theory of planned behaviour accurately predicted intentions to lose weight and that intentions, together with perceived control, accurately predicted weight loss.
the theory of planned behaviour was successful at predicting intentions to lose weight and that intentions to lose weight predicted the actual amount of weight lost.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a theory of planned action that emphasizes the role of perceived control and intentions.
a theory of behavior change and its implications for the treatment of obesity.
the development of a theory of self-control, which may be useful in understanding a variety of behaviors.

the theory of planned behaviour is a useful framework for predicting weight loss in women, but that the role of perceived control in the theory requires further clarification.

weight reduction can be successfully achieved through planning and control.
